extracted.intended_audience: journal peer reviewers assessing Registered Reports (Wiley journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers on assessing Stage 1 (study design) and Stage 2 (completed study) Registered Report submissions, focusing on pre-registered methods, feasibility, adherence, and validity of conclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 manuscript content
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 1 manuscripts will include only an Introduction, Methods (including proposed analyses), and Pilot Data (where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines the expected components reviewers should see at Stage 1 and frames which sections they should evaluate (no Results/Discussion at this stage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of the research question(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: The importance of the research question(s), for journals that normally include this as a criterion for acceptance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess whether the question(s) are meaningful and worthy of publication according to the journal's usual criteria (if applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Logic, rationale, and plausibility of the proposed hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: The logic, rationale, and plausibility of the proposed hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether hypotheses follow logically from background/rationale and are plausible given prior knowledge; assess conceptual soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soundness and feasibility of the methodology and analysis pipeline
rubrics_metrics.description: The soundness and feasibility of the methodology and analysis pipeline (including statistical power analysis where appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the study design and analysis plan are appropriate to test the hypotheses and whether proposed sample sizes/power analyses are adequate; consider practical feasibility before data collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and degree of methodological detail for exact replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the clarity and degree of methodological detail is sufficient to exactly replicate the proposed experimental procedures and analysis pipeline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that all procedural steps, materials, measures, and analysis pipelines are described with enough precision that another researcher could reproduce the study and analyses as pre-registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-specification of outcome-neutral tests (positive controls and quality checks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors have pre-specified sufficient outcome-neutral tests for ensuring that the results obtained are able to test the stated hypotheses, including positive controls and quality checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if the authors planned objective checks (e.g., manipulations/positive controls, data quality assessments) that validate the study can meaningfully test the hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 1 decision consequences and publication of Stage 1 article
rubrics_metrics.description: Following Stage 1 peer review, manuscripts will be accepted, offered the opportunity to revise, or rejected outright. Acceptance of Stage 1 means Stage 2 will be eligible for publication pending successful completion according to pre-registered methods and defensible interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should understand that Stage 1 acceptance is provisional for Stage 2 contingent on adherence to the approved protocol and evidence-based interpretation; Stage 1 articles are published after acceptance (unless embargoed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Stage 2 manuscript content
rubrics_metrics.description: Stage 2 articles, written after study completion, include Results and Discussion sections and more closely resemble a regular article format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines what reviewers will receive at Stage 2 and that their assessment should focus on completed-study material in light of the approved Stage 1 plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether data satisfy approved outcome-neutral conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the data are able to test the authors’ proposed hypotheses by satisfying the approved outcome-neutral conditions (such as quality checks, positive controls).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the pre-specified quality checks and controls indicate the data are valid and suitable to address the hypotheses; failure of these checks can undermine claims regardless of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency with approved Stage 1 (Introduction, rationale, hypotheses)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Introduction, rationale and stated hypotheses are the same as the approved Stage 1 submission (required).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that authors have not substantively changed their hypotheses, rationale, or primary aims from the accepted Stage 1 plan; major deviations require justification and may affect eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to registered experimental procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors adhered precisely to the registered experimental procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the executed procedures match those pre-registered; document and evaluate any deviations and their potential impact on validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification and soundness of unregistered post hoc analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether any unregistered post hoc analyses added by the authors are justified, methodologically sound, and informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Post hoc/exploratory analyses are allowed but should be clearly labeled and their rationale and methods scrutinized for appropriateness; reviewers may suggest additional post hoc tests, but authors are not obliged to perform them unless necessary to meet Stage 2 criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Whether conclusions are justified given the data
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the authors’ conclusions are justified given the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate if interpretations and claims follow from the results (including negative findings); editorial decisions prioritize adherence to approved protocols and data-supported conclusions rather than novelty or perceived importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision principles at Stage 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial decisions will be based on adherence to the approved protocols and experimental design in Stage 1 and conclusions supported by data (even if they are negative findings) as opposed to novelty and perceived importance of results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should apply the principle that fidelity to the registered plan and honest, evidence-based interpretation determine publication, not the direction or novelty of results.
